newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRTRS-S.Australian farmers oppose wool centre closure.
newsitem.headline: RTRTRS-S.Australian farmers oppose wool centre closure.

text.p: The South Australian Farmers Federation said on Monday it continued to oppose moves to close the Adelaide wool selling centre, despite recent talks with the Australian Wool Exchange (AWEX).
"At this stage there is no evidence of any benefits whatsoever to South Australian wool growers (from the proposed closure)," federation livestock executive officer Louise Elleway told Reuters.

"Any benefits to the industry as a whole are marginal, the costs (savings) are probably reasonably marginal as well, but we think to make any such move there have to be substantial benefits," she said.

The federation said AWEX planned to cut Australia's wool selling centres - now located in Fremantle, Sydney, Adelaide, Melbourne, and Geelong - to three centres by July 1997, with Adelaide earmarked as one of those to go.

Elleway said other wool centres had been closed in the past, but Adelaide, with 10 year average receivals at 535,000 bales a year, represented a higher throughput and also handled a broader wooltype, averaging 22-23 microns, than other centres.
The SAFF believed that wool brokers also supported Adelaide's special case position, although wool exporters still supported the AWEX position, she said.
The federation has called on AWEX to introduce its promised new technology at its three main selling centres before raising the issue of closing the Adelaide centre.
"The AWEX position is that innovation and technology would occur after rationalisation," SAFF wool and meat chairman Ian Rowett said in a statement.
"Woolgrowers do not trust this approach," he said.
